title: PrefectHQ/fastmcp — 🚀 The fast, Pythonic way to build MCP servers and clients.
content:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects LLMs to tools and data. FastMCP is a full MCP application framework for servers, clients, and interactive apps. A server starts with ordinary Python:
from fastmcp import FastMCP
mcp = FastMCP("Demo 🚀")
@mcp.tool
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Add two numbers"""
    return a + b
if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
Building an effective MCP application is harder than it looks. FastMCP handles all of it. Declare a tool with a Python function, and the schema, validation, and documentation are generated automatically. Connect to a server with a URL, and transport negotiation, authentication, and protocol lifecycle are managed for you. You focus on your logic, and the MCP part just works: with FastMCP, best practices are built in.
That's why FastMCP is the standard framework for working with MCP. FastMCP 1.0 was incorporated into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024. Today, the actively maintained standalone project is downloaded a million times a day, and some version of FastMCP powers 70% of MCP servers across all languages.
FastMCP has three pillars:
Servers wrap your Python functions into MCP-compliant tools, resources, and prompts. Clients connect to any server with full protocol support. And Apps give your tools interactive UIs rendered directly in the conversation.
Building in TypeScript? FastMCP for TypeScript is the official counterpart, built and maintained by the same team. Same pillars, same ideas, npm install @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts.
Ready to build? Start with the installation guide or jump straight to the quickstart.
FastMCP handles the MCP application layer. FastMCP Gateway is the enterprise MCP gateway for scaling servers and tools across teams, with centralized governance over how they are deployed, discovered, secured, and used.
FastMCP and FastMCP Gateway are built by the same team at Prefect.
Deploy FastMCP servers from GitHub with branch previews and instant rollback. Create a private registry of every MCP your company uses. Secure access with SSO and tool-level RBAC. Get audit logs, observability, and governance across your MCP stack. Remix approved tools into purpose-built endpoints for teams and agents.
Start with FastMCP. Scale with FastMCP Gateway →
We recommend adding FastMCP to your project with uv:
uv add fastmcp
For full installation instructions, including verification and upgrading, see the Installation Guide.
Upgrading? We have guides for:
FastMCP's complete documentation is available at gofastmcp.com, including detailed guides, API references, and advanced patterns.
Documentation is also available in llms.txt format, which is a simple markdown standard that LLMs can consume easily:
- llms.txt is essentially a sitemap, listing all the pages in the documentation.
- llms-full.txt contains the entire documentation. Note this may exceed the context window of your LLM.
Give your coding agent llms.txt as its starting point. See Coding Agents for version-matched documentation and the optional server authoring skill.
Community: Join our Discord server to connect with other FastMCP developers and share what you're building.
Start with CONTRIBUTING.md for accepted contributions and the issue-assignment workflow, then follow the Contributing Guide for setup and validation. Agents should read AGENTS.md.

report.summary: FastMCP, Prefect's Pythonic framework for building MCP servers and clients, now powers roughly 70% of MCP servers and adds an enterprise governance gateway.
report.background: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in late 2024, standardizes how LLM applications connect to external tools, data sources, and prompts — a kind of USB-C port for AI agents. The protocol solved the interface problem, but writing a correct MCP server was still fiddly: you had to hand-author JSON schemas, input validation, docstrings, transport negotiation, authentication, and protocol lifecycle handling. FastMCP emerged as a thin, opinionated Python layer that derived all of that from ordinary type-hinted functions. Its momentum is unusual for a community project: FastMCP 1.0 was merged into the official MCP Python SDK in 2024, and the standalone project has since grown into a full application framework spanning servers, clients, and interactive apps, with a TypeScript sibling. Prefect now positions it as the de facto standard, with a commercial gateway layered on top for organizations running many MCP servers across teams.
key_points: Declarative authoring over boilerplate: you write a normal Python function, decorate it with @mcp.tool, and FastMCP derives the JSON schema, argument validation, and human-readable documentation automatically. Running the server is a single mcp.run() call. The framework's pitch is that MCP best practices — typing, error handling, protocol conformance — are defaults rather than things you remember to add.

Three product pillars: Servers wrap functions into MCP-compliant tools, resources, and prompts; Clients connect to any MCP server with full protocol support including transport negotiation and auth; Apps render interactive UIs directly inside the conversation rather than returning plain text. That last pillar pushes MCP beyond tool-calling into embeddable agent interfaces.

Adoption is the headline: FastMCP 1.0 shipped inside the official MCP Python SDK in 2024, the standalone project sees roughly a million downloads a day, and some version of FastMCP underpins about 70% of MCP servers across all languages. A same-team TypeScript port (@prefecthq/fastmcp-ts) mirrors the design for Node developers.

FastMCP Gateway targets the operational gap: deploying servers from GitHub with branch previews and instant rollback, a private registry of approved MCPs, SSO with tool-level role-based access control, audit logs, observability, and the ability to remix approved tools into purpose-built endpoints for specific teams or agents.

Agent-native documentation: the project publishes llms.txt (a sitemap) and llms-full.txt (the entire docs), plus AGENTS.md and a server-authoring skill, so coding agents can be pointed at version-matched docs. Installation is a single uv add fastmcp, with upgrade guides for breaking releases.
report.impact: For the AI industry, FastMCP looks less like a library and more like the substrate of the tool-use ecosystem. If roughly 70% of MCP servers trace back to one codebase, then its defaults — how schemas are generated, how errors surface, how auth is negotiated — effectively become the protocol's real-world behavior, and Prefect gains unusual leverage over an open standard. For developers, the barrier to shipping an MCP server drops from days to minutes, but it also means MCP servers become commoditized: differentiation shifts to the quality of the underlying tool logic and to governance. The Gateway launch signals where value accrues — registries, access control, auditability, and observability — the same playbook that turned Kubernetes distributions and API gateways into businesses. For end users, the practical effect is more capable, more consistent agent integrations, with interactive in-conversation apps replacing walls of text, alongside new questions about which tools an agent is permitted to touch.
report.tools: Start with FastMCP itself (pip/uv add fastmcp) and the docs at gofastmcp.com, including llms.txt for wiring up a coding agent. TypeScript developers should use @prefecthq/fastmcp-ts. For testing, use the official MCP Inspector and FastMCP's built-in client to exercise servers locally. Pair it with the reference MCP Python SDK to understand the underlying protocol, and connect via Claude Desktop, Cursor, or VS Code for real-world client testing. Watch FastMCP Gateway for multi-server deployments.
